entry.title: Listen To Torture Methods’ Bewitching Dark Realities For The Quasi-Angelic
entry.summary: The opening track from Dark Realities For The Quasi-Angelic — the new album from NYC-based musician Grant Chapman, who releases music under the name Torture Methods — is titled “Rainbow Brite,” but it sounds like we’re entering hell. Or maybe we’re wandering purgatory, battling between the light and dark. Chains rattle into a hypnotic beat,…
entry.content:
The opening track from Dark Realities For The Quasi-Angelic — the new album from NYC-based musician Grant Chapman, who releases music under the name Torture Methods — is titled "Rainbow Brite," but it sounds like we're entering hell. Or maybe we're wandering purgatory, battling between the light and dark. Chains rattle into a hypnotic beat, and a manipulated soul sample floats in the background. There's also a fresh breath of synths, unsettling screams, glittery chimes, and other misplaced vocals. It's the farthest thing from what I would consider the sound of Rainbow Brite, and it's great.

The rest of Dark Realities For The Quasi-Angelic is equally terrifying and enticing. There's dark demon womping and celestial vocal coos on "Cold Pulse," and then there's "Hellmouth," which sounds like a ballad sung by Gollum's cousin. Overall, Dark Realities is a poignant collection of sample-quilted tracks.

On his Bandcamp, Chapman shared that the album is "composed entirely of samples and was written over two months during the summer of ‘26." He added: "This body of work developed around the writings of Mark Fisher and Adam Curtis documentaries. It is heavily inspired by the second wave of Black Metal, the music of Burial as well as the 1998 Sega Saturn game: Baroque."

Listen below.

entry.content:
Last year, Samuel Fenton and Jezmi Tarik Fehmi, both members of London rock group Bar Italia, released Shakedown, the latest album under their Double Virgo moniker. Yesterday, they returned with “City Zen,” their first new music since.

I don’t really smoke cigarettes, but "City Zen" makes me want to. Not that the song explicitly endorses nicotine; there’s just something effortlessly cool and slinky about it that makes it feel like the perfect soundtrack for a drag. Listening to it makes me feel like a spy undercover. Gauzy big beat drums, a heavy, freewheeling bassline and an air of nonchalance give it a kind of smoky, late-night allure.

entry.title: Killers Guitarist Details Recovery From Major Stroke
entry.summary: Killers guitarist Dave Keuning shared both beautiful and terrifying news yesterday. In an Instagram post, Keuning revealed that, three months ago, he and his wife had a baby girl, Odette. Then, a couple of weeks ago, Keuning survived a major stroke. Thankfully, he and his wife were able to rush to the hospital, and he…
entry.content:
Killers guitarist Dave Keuning shared both beautiful and terrifying news yesterday. In an Instagram post, Keuning revealed that, three months ago, he and his wife had a baby girl, Odette. Then, a couple of weeks ago, Keuning survived a major stroke. Thankfully, he and his wife were able to rush to the hospital, and he was immediately taken into surgery. He shared that the doctors said he had "a 40% chance of survival and I would have disabilities after, but by some miracle I am fine."

He added: "I feel extremely fortunate that I am alive and well, and that I can use my hands and feet and talk just like before. I am thankful for my wife, my son, my daughter, and all of my bandmates, who I feel closer to than ever."

We're so glad he's okay. The full post reads:

Happy Thanksgiving, everyone! Three months ago, we had our baby girl, Odette.

Two weeks ago, I had a major stroke, and thanks to my wife acting fast, I went straight to the hospital and into surgery. The first hour after a stroke is critical when it comes to getting to the hospital. I had a blood clot in my brain that cut off the blood supply to the entire right side of my brain. By the time I arrived at the hospital, I was blind in one eye and had lost function on my left side, but I still wasn’t able to realize I was having a stroke. The doctors said I had a 40% chance or survival and I would have disabilities after, but by some miracle I am fine.

And yes I can play guitar just as good as before. It was the first thing I checked when I woke up from surgery.

I feel extremely fortunate that I am alive and well, and that I can use my hands and feet and talk just like before. I am thankful for my wife, my son, my daughter, and all of my bandmates, who I feel closer to than ever.

entry.title: Ginuwine Releases Ridiculous Videogame About Stealing His Masters Back
entry.summary: Move over, GTA VI. Ginuwine just dropped his own absurd videogame, and the two have more in common than you might think. My Ride: The Ginuwine Story Game features plenty of action, music-industry cameos, and a sense of vigilante justice. Though it probably didn’t take more than a decade to make, and it was definitely…
entry.content:
Move over, GTA VI. Ginuwine just dropped his own absurd videogame, and the two have more in common than you might think. My Ride: The Ginuwine Story Game features plenty of action, music-industry cameos, and a sense of vigilante justice. Though it probably didn't take more than a decade to make, and it was definitely made with AI. The game was created by Games By LMG, which also offers a course on making videogames with AI.

In an Instagram post, Ginuwine thanked LMG content creator and developer Anderson Westfield:

Try it out shouts to my folks @lmg2kool you out did yourself king thank you so much , yall play my game this weekend while you wait for me the premise is to get my masters back from my label and live free and get what’s owed to me after over 30 years let’s see how far you make it

Here's the gist: Ginuwine wants his masters back from Sony Music. The game is split into four chapters, in which you must track down a villainous music executive named Mr. Vance, steal the masters back, bring them to the studio, broadcast them to the world, and finally perform for a massive crowd. Along the way, you'll kick plenty of ass and run into familiar faces, including Timbaland, Missy Elliott, Tank, Tweet, and even the ghost of Aaliyah — all of whom were part of the late-'90s R&B and hip-hop collective the Supafriendz.

It's very weird, very easy to play, and quite possibly the most Ginuwine videogame ever made. See videos and images of it below.

entry.content:
Early Nov. 25, Toronto musician Michael Eckert was killed in a home invasion in the South Hill neighborhood. Police arrived at the scene around 2:30 a.m. and found Eckert suffering from a gunshot wound. He was taken to the hospital, where he passed away later that morning. He was 39 years old.

As of Wednesday night, no suspects had been identified. Authorities told reporters that at least one intruder had forced entry into the residence, fired a gun, and then fled the scene.

Eckert was known for being a talented pedal steel and dobro player. He performed under the moniker Neon Eagle and was a member of the ensemble Doghouse Orchestra. He also played with artists such as Blue Rodeo, Billianne, Abigail Lapell, Doug Paisley, Great Lake Swimmers, the Honeyrunners, and more. His death has prompted an outpouring of grief from Toronto's music community, with friends, fellow musicians and collaborators remembering him for his immense talent and the impact he had on those around him.

entry.title: Lana Del Rey Shares Thanksgiving Update On New Albums
entry.summary: Lana Del Rey is grateful and we are grateful for Lana Del Rey. Today, the pop star shared a couple Instagram posts expressing gratitude. One celebrated her collaboration with composer David Arnold on the theme song for the 2026 James Bond video game 007 First Light. They won a Hollywood Music In Media Award. Another…
entry.content:
Lana Del Rey is grateful and we are grateful for Lana Del Rey. Today, the pop star shared a couple Instagram posts expressing gratitude. One celebrated her collaboration with composer David Arnold on the theme song for the 2026 James Bond video game 007 First Light. They won a Hollywood Music In Media Award. Another post was more personal:

Sending love to absolutely everyone today. Thinking of the history of our country and trying to energetically honor so many of the early traditions and culture of the people who were first on this beautiful land. My heart is always with you.

Also grateful to my family who have continued to spend time together for our gatherings, old and new. It’s the glue that keeps me together in this crazy game we call life. Hope we can find one thing to feel grateful for. ?

And that's not all! In the comments, fans were asking about Lana's impending albums, neither of which has a release date yet. She replied that the albums are still in the process of being made but are nearing the end. She sounds very happy with them. Her full comment reads:

Also have to say the albums are coming along so well. I’m happy with them. Taking time cooking but definitely gonna be out at the perfect time considering how much music is on both of them. Definitely getting close to wrapping up although did take so many unexpected turns over the years. Can’t say I saw it coming but what came out of it feels meant to be - it makes me wonder where I would even go after this. So much internal dialogue within ‘you’ve got a friend’ lyrically so much going over what happened in the last three years and why? What are the lessons? Are there any lessons? Is it all on God’s time? Makes me feel like there’s no way the things that happen could be random – one thing that comes to mind is that little quote… You can have it all, but you can’t have it all at the same time

Anyways, don’t fret. I’m so happy with it and when I’m sure it’s finished I’ll tell you – one of the more important things actually with this album is how beautiful the physical copies are, the copper plates alone took half a year to make. it’s an unusual coupling of albums that explain where I started when I announced everything 4 years ago to my perspective now on my internal web of people and their reactions to my happiness and physical growth and success.

“All because I met Happy, who would’ve thought it would make you so mad?”

The follow-up plans to 2023's Did You Know That There's A Tunnel Under Ocean Blvd have been ever-changing and fluid. In 2024, Del Rey announced that she was working on a country album called Lasso with producer Jack Antonoff. That project then evolved to a more Americana album dubbed The Right Person Will Stay, which was expected in May 2025, that birthed the singles "Bluebird" and "Henry, Come On."

The project evolved again, changing its name to Stove. There was no release date given for Stove, but her favorite single "White Feather Hawk Tail Deer Hunter" came out this past February. She worked on it with producers Drew Erickson and Jack Antonoff, mixers Dean Reid and Laura Sisk, and it featured writing contributions from her brother-in-law Jason Pickens, her sister Chuck Grant, and her husband Jeremy Dufrene. Lana recently performed that single while sitting on a stove. Stove has had staying power, and is "intact," but Del Rey has also been working on a companion album. There's no name yet for the accompanying album, but some fans speculate it might be called Spyda.

Check out the full post below, which features a video of her hugging a large tree.

entry.content:
On their latest single, “Queen Cong,” Montreal-based punk band DVTR put it in simple terms: “Fuck that shit,” vocalist Demi Lune sings on the chorus, followed by “Smack me bitch.” There’s more to the lyrics, but they’re in French, and my high school French is too rusty to catch much beyond those words. After some translation, other lyrics take aim at racism and misogyny, at the ways girls are raised to be docile, graceful, and nice, and at the language and tactics used to control people. Yeah, fuck all that shit.

“Queen Cong” is a clanky, restless punk song. Its sound is sort of brass-knuckled Omni — something about the bent guitar riffs. The bass zooms around like a fly on speed, while the chorus explodes into a burst of playful rowdiness.

Check it out below.

entry.content:
Macy Gray, who has always been open to new forms of marketing, is trying something new with her next album rollout. According to Variety, the singer-songwriter is partnering with Singapore-based microdrama app ReelShort to release new music alongside an original scripted vertical drama designed to be watched on your phone. Think of it as a series of bite-sized soap opera episodes built for the scrolling culture of social media. Both the album and the series will reportedly share the same title: The Trouble With The Truth.

The scripted microdrama, which will star Gray, is currently casting. The plan is to release both the album and series in Q1, with production scheduled to begin in January 2027.

ReelShort is the biggest microdrama app, with users reportedly spending nearly 36 minutes a day watching its content. To some, this may be the future of Hollywood; to others, its demise. One scroll through the app's website reveals a catalog loaded with AI-generated or AI-assisted creations. I'd just like to share a few titles: My Ex Called Me Fat, The Vampire Lord Called Me His, My Billionaire Divorce Squad, Bully Me? I Run The Mob, and Crypto Jackpot After Life Failure.

Microdramas first began gaining traction in China during the 2010s, and the business has continued to expand. Deloitte projects that in-app microdrama revenue will reach approximately $7.8 billion in 2026.

This latest venture for Gray follows her stint on The Masked Singer, where she competed in three different countries. Most recently, she appeared on the UK version last year as "Toad In The Hole."

entry.title: U2 Perform Their Dolly Parton Collaboration At First-Ever Thanksgiving Eve NFL Game
entry.summary: Some might say, there’s nothing like turkey and football. Some of those people might say there’s nothing like U2 before turkey and football. And those people probably watched the first Thanksgiving Eve NFL game that happened last night. The game, which aired on Netflix, was between the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams. U2…
entry.content:
Some might say, there's nothing like turkey and football. Some of those people might say there's nothing like U2 before turkey and football. And those people probably watched the first Thanksgiving Eve NFL game that happened last night. The game, which aired on Netflix, was between the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams. U2 performed the halftime show with Best New Artist Grammy nominees the Womack Sisters.

As U2 walked onto the field, a choir eerily recited the lyrics of "I Still Haven't Found What I'm Looking For." The band then began playing "Sunday Bloody Sunday." Later in the song, a drumline came on the field, followed by the Womack Sisters, who sang some of the Supremes' "Stop! In The Name Of Love." It was a cool mix.

As Bono sang the line "The trenches dug within our hearts/ And mothers, children, brothers, sisters torn apart," repeating it twice, U2 transitioned into the live debut of "Torn," the new Dolly Parton collaboration that marks her last vocal recording. As Parton's voice played over speakers, images of her smiling were projected on giant white sheets that hung over the stage.

U2 then played "Where The Streets Have No Name" and finished with "Pride (In The Name Of Love)," once again joined by the Womack Sisters. The Womack Sisters are the daughters of Cecil and Linda Womack, whose own musical project, Womack & Womack, once opened for U2. Linda Womack is also the daughter of soul legend Sam Cooke.

U2 announced their 2027 North American tour a few days ago. Earlier this month they filmed the BBC special U2: Live On The BBC At Tate Modern, premiering on Saturday, and a performance at the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall Of Fame induction ceremony, premiering Dec. 8.

As they reminded Rich Eisen this week, U2 played the Super Bowl almost 25 years ago. Bono called it their "kind of Ed Sullivan moment." He said, "we were just in this bewildering position of trying to put the grief and all the feelings that happened after 9/11 onto, the NFL gave us this opportunity. That was our moment."

Watch clips from the NFL halftime performance below.

entry.content:
We named London art-rock quartet Legss one of the best new artists of 2025 on the strength of their debut album Unreal. Today, they're back with their first new material since then, the slowcore-inspired "Angels Hide (Their Faces)," which the band wrote, rehearsed, and recorded themselves in a home studio that drummer/producer Louis Grace built beneath an abandoned crypt in Bethnal Green.

"The song is an ode to the dual joys and pressures of working in this isolated and symbiotic way together," vocalist Ned Green explains. "A four-headed beast, it is also a duet, a blazing lo-fi embrace, and the first time Louis and I have shared lead vocals together on a song."

Listen to "Angels Hide (Their Faces)" below.

entry.title: Duran Duran’s Andy Taylor Dead At 65
entry.summary: Andy Taylor, guitarist for new wave titans Duran Duran and supergroup the Power Station, has died. Duran Duran announced his passing today in a statement on their website and social media accounts. Taylor died peacefully at home Monday “following a long and courageous battle with prostate cancer.” He was 65. Taylor’s wife Tracey shared this…
entry.content:
Andy Taylor, guitarist for new wave titans Duran Duran and supergroup the Power Station, has died. Duran Duran announced his passing today in a statement on their website and social media accounts. Taylor died peacefully at home Monday "following a long and courageous battle with prostate cancer." He was 65.

Taylor's wife Tracey shared this statement:

To the world, Andy was a brilliant guitarist, but to us, he was the most wonderful husband, a loving dad and the proudest grandfather. He was the rock of our family. For all the incredible experiences music brought him, family always came first. Nothing made him happier than having us all together, and no matter how far music took him, his heart was always at home.

Andy faced the last few years with so much courage and determination. He never gave up, fighting until the very end, never losing his love of life. The kindness and support shown to him by fans from all over the world throughout his illness brought him immense comfort and strength, and for that we will always be grateful.

Andy knew just how deeply he was loved, and we take great comfort in that. We will miss him every single day.

Duran Duran offered these words:

Andy was there at the very beginning of our story. From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music. His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed.

It was great to make music with him again when the original five reunited in the early 2000s, and that time together, both on stage and in the studio, meant a tremendous amount to all of us. When we were inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2022, Andy was too unwell to join us, but his words that night reminded everyone of his strength and the bond we shared.

Andy faced his illness with remarkable courage, honesty and grace.

Our thoughts are with his wife Tracey, his children Georgina, Isabella, Bethany and Andrew, and grandson Albie. They all loved him deeply and we ask that their privacy be respected at this very difficult time.  In lieu of flowers, the family has asked that donations be made in Andy’s name to Prostate Cancer UK: prostatecanceruk.org.

With love from Simon, John, Nick and Roger.

Taylor was born in 1961 in the coastal English town of Tynemouth. He began playing guitar at 11 and joined bands as a teenager, dropping out of school to tour. In 1980 he moved to Birmingham, where he met and joined a fledgling Duran Duran. Taylor played a key role in developing the group's sound, a poppy, glammed-out mix of post-punk and disco that put the group at the forefront of the New Romantic movement.

Taylor played on Duran Duran's first three albums, helping them to become global superstars with a streak of hits including "Girls On Film," "Rio," "Hungry Like The Wolf," and "The Reflex." In 1985, while Duran Duran were on hiatus, Taylor and the group's bassist John Taylor (no relation) formed a new band called the Power Station with singer Robert Palmer and Chic drummer Tony Thompson. The Power Station released their debut album in 1985, achieving worldwide success as well. When Duran Duran reconvened to record 1986's Notorious, Taylor had lost interest in their style, preferring to play rock 'n' roll. He left the band during the making of the album to pursue a solo career in his new home base of Los Angeles.

Taylor had a solo hit in 1986 with "Take It Easy" from the movie American Anthem. Over the next decade, he released two solo albums, made a second album with the Power Station, and worked closely with Rod Stewart on two of Stewart's albums. In the early 2000s, he teamed with the classic Duran Duran lineup to record the comeback album Astronaut and mount a successful reunion tour. He continued to perform and record with the band for several years before departing again in 2006.

In 2018, Taylor was diagnosed with stage 4 prostate cancer, an illness that prevented him from being there when Duran Duran were inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall Of Fame in 2022. But he did contribute to the group's 2023 album Danse Macabre, while also releasing two recent solo albums. Taylor's death comes weeks after drummer Roger Taylor (also no relation) retired from Duran Duran due to tinnitus. He is survived by Tracey, his wife of 44 years, and four children.

Born in 1942, Giles got his start playing in bands with his bassist brother…
entry.content:
Michael Giles, the original drummer of English prog-rock titans King Crimson, has died. Discipline Global Mobile, the record label founded by his old bandmate Robert Fripp, shared the news today, confirming that Giles passed away on Nov. 23. He was 84.

Born in 1942, Giles got his start playing in bands with his bassist brother Peter. When they posted a newspaper advertisement looking for a keyboardist who could sing, they instead found Robert Fripp, a guitarist who couldn't. Nevertheless, they formed the trio of Giles, Giles & Fripp, signing to Deram and releasing a lone album, The Cheerful Insanity of Giles, Giles & Fripp, in 1968.

Following the addition of multi-instrumentalist Ian McDonald and the departure of Peter Giles, the group morphed into the first incarnation of King Crimson, rounded out by bassist/vocalist Greg Lake and lyricist Peter Sinfield. Michael Giles played on their landmark 1969 debut In The Court Of The Crimson King before leaving the band, although he still contributed to their 1970 follow-up In The Wake Of Poseidon.

Giles briefly formed a duo with fellow former King Crimson member Ian McDonald, releasing the self-titled album McDonald And Giles in 1970. He then transitioned into a successful career as a session musician, working with acts including Steve Winwood, Bryan Ferry, Leo Sayer, Anthony Phillips, Kevin Ayers, Greg Lake, Neil Sedaka, Yvonne Elliman, Rupert Hine, Roger Glover, Francis Monkman, Andy Summers, Peter Sinfield, and the Penguin Cafe Orchestra.

In 2001, Giles released his first solo album, Progress. A year later, he co-founded the 21st Century Schizoid Band, performing material from King Crimson's early period with other ex-members. He released his most recent solo album, Shadows/Solo, earlier this year.

entry.content:
Ace Stallings is a familiar face on the national hardcore circuit. I know him a little bit — great guy. In addition to promoting shows and doing the interview podcast Forum Of Passion, Stallings has fronted a ton of bands: Break Away, Mutually Assured Destruction, Sentinel, Eliminators. In 2024, Stallings launched Rose Chamber, a project different from any he'd done before.

Rose Chamber, named after a great Mutually Assured Destruction song, is the duo of Stallings and Evan Schlomann, his bandmate in Sentinel. (Schlomann has also been in bands like Casket Architects and Night Terrors.) They make cold, mean, gothed-out synthpop, and Stallings' Danzig-esque bellow sounds really cool over that kind of music.

Rose Chamber already released the 2024 EP State Of Affairs and Double Feature, a 2025 split with the Shape. All of the tracks on those records will appear on Rose Chamber's full-length debut My Silhouette, along with new tracks like the awesomely mean opener "Modern Rot." As someone who writes a column about the Billboard Modern Rock chart, I appreciate that title. Check out the "Modern Rot" video below.

03 "No Sanctuary"

My Silhouette is out 1/22 on Avant! Records.

entry.title: Anna Meredith – “Mink”
entry.summary: Listen to Scottish composer Anna Meredith's new song "Mink" from her upcoming studio album 'DARLING,' the follow-up to 2019's 'FIBS.'
entry.content:
Fresh off of her score for Wicker, the heavily memed film in which Academy Award winner Olivia Colman fucks a man made out of wicker played by Alexander Skarsgård, Scottish composer Anna Meredith is returning with her first official studio album since 2019's FIBS. DARLING will be out in February, and we've already heard its bright and frenetic opening track and lead single "Dusky." Follow-up "Mink" is calmer but no less imposing, a cresting wave of strings and synths. Meredith explains:

To me "Mink" is the "heart" of the album and a very different kind of intensity to lots of the other music. As with so much of the material, it’s the blend of the electronics and acoustic instruments that I hope gives it its sonic identity. In "Mink" the idea is a bending, pulsing core which is set within these massive synth chords right from the opening but this sinew-y pulsed idea grows and grows in power, infecting the rest of the instruments. The peak of the track grows to this exaggerated, intense almost strobe-like idea of what started as a smaller thread. We recorded this track with a string ensemble made from incredibly talented friends (and the best string players I know). I’m so grateful to them for such beautiful playing.

The track has a performance video from longtime collaborator Ewan Jones Morris filmed at Lightroom in King's Cross. Watch and listen below.

DARLING is out 2/12 via Mercury KX. Pre-order it here.

entry.title: Manchester Police Say Don Toliver Concert Gas Incident May Be Linked To Jewelry Thefts
entry.summary: On Sunday night, the newly dominant rap star Don Toliver performed for an audience of 12,000 at Manchester’s Co-op Live, but the show descended into chaos. Midway through Toliver’s performance, police evacuated the arena after people in the crowd breathed what cops describe as an “unknown substance,” widely believed to be tear gas. The show…
entry.content:
On Sunday night, the newly dominant rap star Don Toliver performed for an audience of 12,000 at Manchester's Co-op Live, but the show descended into chaos. Midway through Toliver's performance, police evacuated the arena after people in the crowd breathed what cops describe as an "unknown substance," widely believed to be tear gas. The show never restarted, and Toliver postponed two planned gigs at London's O2 Arena in the aftermath. Now, Manchester police claim that the tear-gassing incident could've been linked to a few jewelry robberies that reportedly took place during the show.

In a statement on their website yesterday, Manchester police said:

As part of progressing enquiries, detectives are exploring the possibility that release of the substance could be linked to reports of a small number of robbery offences at the arena on Sunday evening.

It comes after we received nine reports of jewellery being stolen during the same concert. No arrests have been made at this time.

As part of that statement, Assistant Chief Constable Tom Harding says, "We are aware similar robberies have been reported at two European concerts for the same artist and will be linking in with our European counterparts to better understand the wider picture of this suspected offending."

Chain-snatchings at rap shows are nothing new, but apparently some thieves also use pepper spray or tear gas to set off panicked reactions in crowded spaces and make it easier to grab other people's stuff. After the 2017 terrorist attack that killed 22 people at an Ariana Grande show, arena concerts in Manchester must be awfully tense. I'm sure that makes it easier to start a panic, and that also makes it an even more despicable thing to do.

Yesterday, Co-op Live posted their own statement, saying that they've learned there's "no ongoing risk" from that evacuation and that all scheduled concerts at the venue will happen as planned.

On Monday, Toliver posted about the incident and his postponed London shows on his Instagram story, writing, "The only thing I love more than creating music is performing for my Fans ! STOP BRING BULLSHIT INTO MY SHOWS!! it ain’t Cool see you soon London. Love you Guys."

entry.title: Vince Staples Covers A Geto Boys Classic In The BBC Live Lounge
entry.summary: You don’t see too many rappers doing cover songs. Rap is too subjective for that, too focused on projection of the self. Samples and quotes and allusions are one thing, but covers are another. Vince Staples doesn’t care. Staples covered the Geto Boys’ unimpeachable 1991 classic “Mind Playing Tricks On Me” on a recent visit…
entry.content:
You don't see too many rappers doing cover songs. Rap is too subjective for that, too focused on projection of the self. Samples and quotes and allusions are one thing, but covers are another. Vince Staples doesn't care. Staples covered the Geto Boys' unimpeachable 1991 classic "Mind Playing Tricks On Me" on a recent visit to the BBC Live Lounge, taking a deeply familiar track and putting a different spin on it. He made the song his own. That's what a cover is supposed to be.

Earlier this year, Staples released his Loma Vista debut Cry Baby, an album that gets into indie rock sonics without really altering Staples' point of view. He's touring with a live band. In his Live Lounge session, Staples and his band did the Cry Baby tracks "White Flag" and "Cotton." Then, they took on "Mind Playing Tricks On Me," a song that's two years older than Staples himself. For many of us, "Mind Playing Tricks" is the song we might find ourselves absentmindedly rapping word-for-word, getting to the Willie D verse before we even realize what we're doing. It's a bit like a folk song in that way.

For the Live Lounge performance, Staples' band worked up a supremely laid-back version of the "Mind Playing Tricks" beat. Staples rapped the whole song with reverence, though he took out all the cusswords for some reason. (Can you not cuss in the Live Lounge?) But where the Geto Boys hit every word with wild early-'90s levels of emphasis, Staples just kind of sleepily murmurs the verses. It sounds nice! Watch the full Live Lounge performance below.

Cry Baby is out now on Loma Vista.

entry.title: Watch Erykah Badu’s Weird, Great Fallon Performance

entry.content:
It took forever, but we finally got a new Erykah Badu album this year. Badu and the Alchemist joined forces to release the lovely, spaced-out, singular collaborative LP Before The World Blows, and if you're looking for reasons to be thankful tomorrow, there's one for you. One of the nice things about a new Erykah Badu album is that it put her back on TV, and that's what happened on Jimmy Fallon's Tonight Show on Tuesday.

As far as I can tell, Badu's appearance on last night's Fallon was her first time playing late-night TV in nearly nine years. She really made an event of it, too. Badu sang the Before The World Blows track "Breezy," an affectionate ode to a girl in a car, and she went all-out with her staging.

For nearly half of the song, last night's performance was a tight close-up on Badu in a blonde wig and a brown '70s-looking suit, holding a steering wheel and pretending to drive. The outfit might be a cinematic reference, but I'm not sure. Behind her, a screen made it look a bit like she was driving through a blurry cityscape, then floating in a pink bubble over a CGI skyline.

Halfway through, when the "Bennie And The Jets" sample came in, the screen dropped away and showed Badu's backing band, sans Alchemist. It's a little weird to see Badu playing Fallon without the Roots, her old comrades, but she and her band are all the way locked in right now. Watch the performance below.

Before The World Blows is out now on Control FREAQ Records/Young Recordings.

entry.content:
Last year, the Australian dance/hyperpop producer Ninajirachi released her utterly charming album I Love My Computer. It was one of our favorite records of 2025, and Ninajirachi was one of our favorite new artists. Since then, Ninajirachi has taken the fuck off, playing to big rooms and rapturous festival crowds. Along the way, she's gotten to know a lot of her contemporaries. Today, she's back with a remix album called I Love My Computer, All My Friends Are Inside It.

There are 20 remixes on I Love My Computer, All My Friends Are Inside It, but not all of them are new. Since she put out the original I Love My Computer, Ninajirachi has dropped remixes from acts like Frost Children, underscores, Madeon, Effy, horsegiirL, and 100 gecs' Dylan Brady. I Love My Computer, All My Friends Are Inside It collects all those reworkings, as well as new ones from acts like Wet Leg, Slayr, Genesis Owusu, DJ_Dave, Nikki Nair, nate sib and kimj, and Mallrat. It's fun to hear those tracks explored from all those different angles. In a press release, Ninajirachi says:

Most of my time making music is spent alone, so hearing these songs reimagined by an amazing lineup of artists has been really inspiring and emotional. For an album that was written about experiences I’ve had all on my own, I Love My Computer has connected me to people all around the world more than anything else ever has. It is hard to be eloquent about the time I’ve had with it. It’s just so cool. Literally right now I’m in Mexico City, and I’ve met new people this week that I would’ve never met without music and the internet. There is no time I’d rather be alive than right now. I’m so grateful to the artists for bringing so much of themselves to every new version. Some are new friends, some I've known since I released my first song as Ninajirachi. We've played shows together and been in the studio together, but we all found each other's music on the computer first.

Listen to the remix album below.

I Love My Computer, All My Friends Are Inside It is out now on NLV.

entry.title: Helena Deland – “Whole Life”
entry.summary: A chilly, sleepy morning just before a major holiday is an ideal time to hear a new song from Helena Deland. (Deland is Canadian, so I guess it’s not the day before a major holiday for her, but nevermind.) Early next year, Deland will release Eternity Shrugs, the follow-up to her lovely 2023 album Goodnight…
entry.content:
A chilly, sleepy morning just before a major holiday is an ideal time to hear a new song from Helena Deland. (Deland is Canadian, so I guess it's not the day before a major holiday for her, but nevermind.) Early next year, Deland will release Eternity Shrugs, the follow-up to her lovely 2023 album Goodnight Summerland. We've already posted her songs "How Do You Like Me Now" and "Tip Of My Tongue," and she's got a new one out today.

Deland's latest single is a short, soft, comfy acoustic number called "Whole Life." It's all about finding meaning when you meet someone else and maybe accepting that that's a temporary thing. In a press release, Deland says, "It’s hard to tell, from within something, what it will come to mean in the scope of one’s whole life. The song is about wanting to take in something that is bound to be short-lived. It weighs the denial and magical thinking required to keep a fragile thing going, and lives in the space between ‘Tell me’ and ‘Don’t tell me now,’ wanting to know, knowing already." Listen below.

Eternity Shrugs is out 1/22 on Chivi Chivi.
